title: Timebox tombstones and reversible pseudomap workflow for analytics retention
creator: Priya Malhotra
description: We need a robust, auditable retention workflow for console analytics that balances compliance (right-to-be-forgotten, GDPR CCPA) with operational needs (debugging, product analytics). This ticket proposes a timebox-based tombstone approach combined with reversible pseudonymization mapping stored in a locked KMS-encrypted store for the retention window, followed by an irreversible scrub job after the retention period. The goal is to: 1) allow short-term debugging and rollback by authorized SRE/PMO while minimizing PII exposure; 2) provide cryptographic auditability that data was removed; 3) keep pipeline performance and query latency within SLOs. This complements existing ephemeral-id mapping work but introduces a retention lifecycle, per-tenant flags, and an audit trail for regulators.
acceptance_criteria:
- New tombstone lifecycle field exists on analytics events and is respected by pipeline processors.
- Events older than configured retention (default 90 days) are scrubbed irreversibly from storage and compacted topics within the scrub window.
- Reversible pseudomap accessible only to authorized, audited service accounts for duration of retention; access is logged and visible in audit UI.
- Audit report generation proves that a given event and its reversible mapping were removed after scrub.
- No significant regression in ingest throughput (<5% overhead) or query latency (<50ms p50 impact).
- Feature flag per-tenant allows gradual rollout and emergency rollback.
implementation_notes: High-level plan: 1) Data model: add tombstone_status (active | tombstoned | scrubbed), tombstone_at timestamp, pseudomap_key_id reference. 2) Ingest: producer annotates events when user requests deletion or retention policy hits; tombstone events written to a dedicated tombstone topic with compaction enabled. 3) Pseudomap: create a secure, KMS-encrypted store (e.g., secure-s3 + envelope encryption) that holds reversible pseudonymous IDs mapped to original identifiers; each entry has TTL aligned to retention window. 4) Background jobs: a) tombstone-aggregator compacts per-tenant windows and batches scrub candidates; b) scrub-worker performs irreversible scrub by issuing removal across sinks (bigquery/warehouse partitions, clickhouse tables, topic compaction markers) and deletes corresponding pseudomap entries; c) audit-generator emits signed deletion receipts. 5) Access controls: only the scrub-worker and audit-generator can decrypt pseudomap entries; operations access via privileged RBAC with approval flow. 6) Migration/backfill: create a backfill job for historical PII to convert to tombstoned records and create pseudomap entries for a short grace period. 7) Schema migration via migrations service with forward/backward compatibility.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): implement tombstone field, tombstone topic, and pseudomap prototype in staging; run synthetic retention jobs and verify audit receipts.
- Phase 2 (shadow): enable on a small subset of internal tenants (10%) in shadow mode where scrubs are simulated but not permanently removed; compare results with baseline.
- Phase 3 (canary): enable actual scrubs for internal tenants and 1-2 low-risk customers behind a feature flag. Monitor for errors and customer impact.
- Phase 4 (gradual): ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over multiple cycles, with option to pause per-tenant.
- Emergency rollback: feature flag to stop scrub-workers and rehydrate pseudomap keys from backups if needed.
- Regulatory audit: run end-to-end deletion receipt generation for 5 sample requests across tenants to validate compliance artifacts.
monitoring_metrics:
- tombstone_events_created_total (by tenant)
- scrub_candidates_queued_total
- scrub_success_total / scrub_failure_total (with error reasons)
- pseudomap_entries_active_count
- pseudomap_deletions_total
- audit_receipts_emitted_total
- scrub_job_latency_p50/p95/p99
- downstream_query_error_rate_during_scrub
- ingest_throughput_delta_vs_baseline
- unauthorized_pseudomap_access_attempts
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for tombstone lifecycle logic and pseudomap encryption/decryption.
- Integration tests: end-to-end pipeline in staging that creates tombstone, runs scrub-worker, and verifies data removed from warehouse and compacted topics.
- Property tests: randomness and key rotation for pseudomap to ensure no determinism leaks.
- Chaos tests: kill scrub-worker mid-run to test idempotency and resume semantics.
- Compliance tests: generate signed deletion receipts and validate signature verification flow.
- Performance tests: synthetic load to measure ingest and query impact at 1x/5x baseline traffic.
migration_steps: 1) Create pseudomap storage with KMS key and service principal. 2) Launch a controlled backfill job to convert historical PII into tombstoned format for records within max-retention window; this job annotates pseudomap entries. 3) Gradually flip feature flag for new deletions to go through tombstone path. 4) After stabilization, run bulk scrub for records past retention with a monitored dry-run before irreversible deletes. 5) Rotate pseudomap keys and delete old keys after verifying entries have been removed. 6) Update docs and notify customers about retention behavior and opt-out process.

2026-02-18 Evan Chen: Spiked pseudomap prototype using envelope encryption + DynamoDB TTL. Observed acceptable decrypt latency (~2ms per lookup) when batched. Noting potential cost at high cardinality; exploring compacted topic approach to avoid constant lookups in hot paths.

2026-02-24 Sarah Lopez (Privacy): Confirmed that audit receipts must include signed tombstone_at and scrubed_at timestamps and key fingerprint. Also requested retention window be configurable per-tenant with min/ max bounds.

2026-03-08 DevOps: Provisioned KMS key and secure-s3 bucket for pseudomap prototype. Need to finalize IAM role for scrub-worker and audit-generator.
